output.normalized_title: database-primary: Expired OAuth certificate on identity-provider (database-primary)

output.classification_reasoning: The primary symptom is an expired OAuth certificate on the identity-provider, which directly impacts authentication flows for the database-primary service. This is not a simple network glitch nor a pure application bug; it requires coordination between the identity provider, certificate lifecycle management, and the database service's authentication mechanisms. Resolving it typically involves renewing the certificate, updating trust stores, and possibly rolling out configuration changes across dependent services, indicating a moderate level of operational effort and cross‑component impact.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Do not terminate primary node without promoting read-replica first. Verify write freeze before any restart.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Historical incident INC-1007 matches current symptoms and error signature, indicating a recurring authentication certificate expiration issue on database-primary.

output.governing_sla_rule: Minor disruption impacting < 100 users with standard SLA.
output.justification: The incident impacts 25 users, well below the 100‑user threshold for a minor disruption. The outage duration is 12 minutes, which falls within the acceptable window for Tier‑1 services under the standard SLA. The diagnostic stage is "Root Cause Confirmed" with a high confidence score (0.95), confirming the issue is a recurring authentication certificate expiration on the primary database. According to corporate severity thresholds, these parameters map to SEV-4.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has root access or the ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us-east-1.
verification: AWS identity matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context string contains prod-us-east-1
Master node list is non‑empty

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary
remediation_steps.description: Safely promote the existing read‑replica to become the new primary database before any certificate changes on the current primary.
commands: kubectl exec -n db $(kubectl get pod -l app=database-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- /bin/sh -c "pg_ctl promote"
kubectl label pod $(kubectl get pod -l app=database-replica -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role=primary --overwrite
verification: New primary pod reports role=primary label
pg_isready returns "accepting connections" on the promoted instance
Read‑replica metrics show zero lag

remediation_steps.title: Rotate Expired OAuth Certificate
remediation_steps.description: Upload a fresh OAuth certificate to the identity provider and inject it into the new primary database configuration.
verification: kubectl get pods -l app=database-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[0].ready}' returns true for all pods
curl -sSf https://database-primary.internal/auth/healthz returns HTTP 200 with "cert_valid": true
Log search for ERR_AUTHENTICATION_ISSUE_818 returns zero occurrences in the last 5 minutes

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Confirm overall service health, replication status, and that user traffic is restored.
commands: kubectl exec -n db $(kubectl get pod -l app=database-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;"
verification: Active connections count matches expected baseline (< 5 idle connections)
Health endpoint returns status OK
Service endpoint resolves to the newly promoted primary IP

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: If any verification step fails, revert the certificate change, demote the promoted replica, and roll back the deployment to the previous image tag.

steps.description: Revert OAuth certificate to previous version
commands: aws ssm get-parameter --name /prod/db/oauth_cert_previous --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text > previous_oauth_cert.pem
verification: curl -sSf https://database-primary.internal/auth/healthz returns HTTP 200 with "cert_valid": false (expected failure) confirming old cert is active

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica and restore original primary
commands: kubectl exec -n db $(kubectl get pod -l app=database-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- /bin/sh -c "pg_ctl stop -m immediate"
kubectl label pod $(kubectl get pod -l app=database-replica -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role=primary --overwrite
kubectl label pod $(kubectl get pod -l app=database-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role=replica --overwrite
verification: Original primary pod reports role=replica
Replica pod reports role=primary
pg_isready succeeds on the restored primary

steps.description: Undo deployment rollout to previous image tag
verification: kubectl describe deployment/database-primary | grep Image shows previous tag
Pods return to READY state within 2 minutes

final_verification: Confirm no ERR_AUTHENTICATION_ISSUE_818 entries in logs for the past 15 minutes
Stakeholder sign‑off that service is back to baseline performance

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified (root or ProdOperations SSO)
Current certificate backup stored in SSM at /prod/db/oauth_cert_previous
Read‑replica is healthy and in sync (replication lag < 5s)
safety_verification.notes: All steps are documented, reversible, and include verification checkpoints before proceeding to the next step.
